rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأزهري
rows.claim: They treat waraʾ as a word with opposite senses, meaning either before or behind.
rows.anchor: وراء من الأضداد قاله: أبو عبيدة والأزهري

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Waraʾ names whatever is concealed from someone, whether it lies ahead or behind.
rows.anchor: اسم لما توارى عنك، سواء كان أمامك أم خلفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes waraʾ as behind the person, in pursuit, or as something that will come later.
rows.anchor: بمعنى من خلفه أي: في طلبه كما تقول الأمر من ورائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusqā can coordinate with an omitted verb, ‘he is cast into it,’ or with the governing element of min warāʾihi, functioning as a descriptive clause.
rows.anchor: معطوف على محذوف تقديره: يلقى فيها ويسقى، أو معطوف على العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is parsed as the subject of the passive verb; the apparent sense is that the drink is real water.
rows.anchor: وارتفاع جهنم على الفاعلية، والظاهر إرادة حقيقة الماء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He treats ṣadīd as an adjective of water, while explaining that it is not literally water but is called water by customary usage as its substitute.
rows.anchor: هو نعت لماء، كما تقول: هذا خاتم حديد وليس بماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted comparison: it is like pus, rather than pus itself.
rows.anchor: نعت على إسقاط أداة التشبيه كما تقول: مررت برجل أسد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He analyzes ṣadīd as explanatory apposition to the indefinite māʾ; Abū Ḥayyān notes Basran grammarians reject such apposition with indefinites, unlike Kufans and al-Fārisī.
rows.anchor: صديد عطف بيان لماء قال: ويسقى من ماء، فأبهمه إبهاما، ثم بينه بقوله: صديد

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: He parses ṣadīd as an adjective qualifying water.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: صديد نعت لماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify ṣadīd as fluid running from the bodies of Hell's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: هو ما يسيل من أجساد أهل النار

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والربيع
rows.claim: They identify it as the washings of Hell's inhabitants in Hell.
rows.anchor: هو غسالة أهل النار في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says it is fluid running from the private parts of adulterers, male and female.
rows.anchor: ما يسيل من فروج الزناة والزواني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical explanation derives ṣadīd from turning away: it is repellent pus from which people recoil.
rows.anchor: صديد بمعنى مصدود عنه أي: لكراهته يصد عنه

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the drink is brought near reluctantly; it burns the face and scalp, then cuts the intestines until they exit the drinker's rear. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: يقرب إليه فيتكرهه، فإذا أدني منه شوى وجهه ووقعت فروة رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatajarraʿuhu means that he forces himself to swallow it.
rows.anchor: يتجرعه يتكلف جرعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of lā yakādu yusīghuhu is that he does not even come close to swallowing it; if that approach is absent, swallowing itself is absent.
rows.anchor: ولا يكاد يسيغه أي: ولا يقارب أن يسيغه، فكيف تكون الإساغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with ‘he almost did not see it’ explains that denial of near occurrence entails denial of occurrence.
rows.anchor: فيكون كقوله: لم يكد يراها أي لم يقرب من رؤيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the quoted report ‘then he drinks it’ is sound, the meaning is that he nearly cannot swallow it before eventually drinking, as the slaughtered cow was nearly not slaughtered before it was done.
rows.anchor: فإن صح الحديث كان المعنى: ولا يكاد يسيغه قبل أن يشربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tajarraʿa may express following an action, effort, doing something gradually, or the same meaning as the simple verb.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل هنا وجوها أن يكون للمطاوعة أي جرعه فتجرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatajarraʿuhu can syntactically modify the preceding phrase, be circumstantial from the pronoun in yusqā, or stand as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: يتجرعه صفة لما قبله، أو حال من ضمير ويسقى، أو استئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death coming from every place means its causes; apparently it comes from the six directions, intensifying the terrible suffering.
rows.anchor: ويأتيه الموت أي: أسبابه. والظاهر أن قوله: من كل مكان معناه من الجهات الست

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: He explains ‘from every place’ as from every part of the body, even the tips of its hair; another report extends it to the big toes.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم التيمي: من كل مكان من جسده، حتى من أطراف شعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage apparently describes the Hereafter; al-Akhfash's reading of worldly afflictions metaphorically called death is unlikely because the context concerns Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أراد البلايا التي تصيب الكافر في الدنيا، سماها موتا وهذا بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the drinker is not dead refers to the prolonged severity and duration of death's agonies.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وما هو بميت لتطاول شدائد الموت، وامتداد سكراته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He takes the next punishment as ever-facing and progressively harsher at each moment.
rows.anchor: في كل وقت يستقبله يتلقى عذابا أشد مما قبله وأغلظ

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: He interprets the thick punishment as cutting off and constraining breaths inside bodies.
rows.anchor: هو قطع الأنفاس وحبسها في الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One opinion makes the pronoun in ‘behind it’ refer to the preceding punishment, rather than to every tyrant.
rows.anchor: الضمير في ورائه هو يعود على العذاب المتقدم لا على كل جبار

none: Qurʾānic verse text only; no commentary point is stated.

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: He defines ash as matter pulverized by burning into dust, gives the plural forms r-m-d and armida, notes the rare armidāʾ, and says ramād ramadd is the finest, lightest dust.
rows.anchor: هو جسم يسحقه الإحراق سحق الغبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazaʿ is inability to endure hardship, the opposite of patience; a poem illustrates the word mujzaʿan.
rows.anchor: الجزع: عدم احتمال الشدة، وهو نقيض الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muṣrik is a rescuer; a poem uses the word for one who can give aid.
rows.anchor: فلا تجزعوا إني لكم غير مصرخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣārikh is the one crying for help; Salāma ibn Jandal's verse illustrates the noun and the root's verbal forms include crying, making oneself cry, and calling for aid.
rows.anchor: صرخ يصرخ صرخا وصراخا وصرخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarīkh is a verbal noun that can describe either the helper or the person seeking help, making it a word of opposite senses.
rows.anchor: والصريخ مصدر كالتريخ ويوصف به المغيث والمستغيث من الأضداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farʿ means a tree branch, offspring, or abundant hair; Imruʾ al-Qays's poem uses it for hair.
rows.anchor: ويطلق على ما يولد من الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtuththa means uprooted, jath means pulled out, and juththa means a person's body whether seated or standing; Laqīṭ al-Iyārī's line witnesses the first usage.
rows.anchor: اجتث الشيء اقتلعه، وجث الشيء قلعه، والجثة شخص الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bawār means destruction; a poem illustrates the noun in the phrase fearing destruction.
rows.anchor: غداة الحرب إذ خيف البوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase begins with mathal as a subject whose predicate is omitted, estimated as ‘in what is recited to you’ or ‘is being told,’ following Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: ارتفاع مثل على الابتداء، وخبره محذوف تقديره عند سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal is metaphorical for an unusual quality; ‘their deeds are like ash’ is a resumed answer to an implied question about their likeness.
rows.anchor: والمثل مستعار للصفة التي فيها غرابة، وأعمالهم كرماد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He reports the Kisaʾī and al-Farrāʾ analysis that mathal is suspended, yielding ‘those who disbelieved: their deeds are like ash.’
rows.anchor: ومذهب الكسائي والفراء أنه على إلغاء مثل

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: He makes mathal the subject, aʿmāluhum an encompassing بدل, and ka-ramād the predicate, citing a poetic construction as a parallel.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: مثل رفع بالابتداء، وأعمالهم بدل من مثل بدل اشتمال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He offers deeds as a بدل of ‘the likeness of those who disbelieve,’ with an implied ‘the likeness of their deeds,’ and ka-ramād as predicate.
rows.anchor: أعمالهم بدلا من مثل الذين كفروا على تقدير: مثل أعمالهم، وكرماد الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He prefers treating mathal and aʿmāluhum as successive subjects, with ‘like ash’ predicating the latter and the whole clause predicating the former; their deeds vanish when needed like wind-scattered ash.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي أرجح الأقوال، وكأنك قلت: المتحصل مثالا في النفس للذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the analysis Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers: the clause lacks a link to mathal and is not identical in meaning to it.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول الذي رجحه ابن عطية قال الحوفي، وهو لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' seemingly good deeds—kinship, freeing captives, hospitality, helping the distressed, and protection—come to nothing because they lacked knowledge of God, faith, and action for Him.
rows.anchor: وأعمال الكفرة المكارم التي كانت لهم من صلة الأرحام، وعتق الرقاب

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read al-rīyāḥ in the plural; most readers read al-rīḥ in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع، وأبو جعفر: الرياح على الجمع، والجمهور على الإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the day stormy transfers an adjective of wind to the day by figurative usage, as in expressions such as a day that is sun-dark and sun-eclipsed.
rows.anchor: ووصف اليوم بقوم عاصف، وإن كان من صفة الريح على سبيل التجوز

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: He supplies ‘wind’ after ‘stormy day,’ deleted because wind was already mentioned; a poem likewise means a day whose sun is dark and eclipsed.
rows.anchor: وقال الهروي: التقدير في يوم عاصف الريح، فحذف لتقدم ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical explanation makes ʿāṣif an adjective of wind placed after day and genitive by attraction, as in ‘a lizard hole that is ruined.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: عاصف من صفة الريح، إلا أنه لما جاء بعد اليوم أتبع إعرابه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر عن الحسن
rows.claim: They read ‘in a day of storm,’ construing the adjective as standing for an omitted noun: a day of a violent wind.
rows.anchor: في يوم عاصف على إضافة اليوم لعاصف، وهو على حذف الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān refers readers to the explanation of ʿaṣf in Yūnus, at the phrase ‘a raging wind struck it.’
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير العصوف في يونس في قوله: جاءتها ريح عاصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On allowing a noun to be annexed to its adjective, the reading can mean that on Judgment Day disbelievers find no reward or trace from their works, like scattered ash.
rows.anchor: لا يقدرون يوم القيامة مما كسبوا من أعمالهم على شيء، أي: لا يرون له أثرا من ثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation supplies an omitted word: they cannot obtain any reward from what they earned.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يقدرون من ثواب ما كسبوا، فهو على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the new creation as other human beings of the same kind; a possibility of a different kind is also mentioned, but Abū Ḥayyān says the former is the only tenable reading, as in 4:133.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل من غير جنسكم. والأول قول جمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing people with a new creation is neither impossible nor difficult for God, who can do whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: وما ذهابكم والإتيان بخلق جديد بممتنع ولا متعذر عليه تعالى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He argues that God is intrinsically capable of every possible object; once an unopposed motive directs Him, action follows without delay, like moving one's finger.
rows.anchor: لأنه قادر الذات لا اختصاص له بمقدور دون مقدور، فإذا خلص له الداعي إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān identifies a Muʿtazilī insinuation in Zamakhsharī's distinction between divine being capable and having power, and in comparing God's act to a person's finger movement; human movement also occurs only by God's power, while human capacity does not create anything.
rows.anchor: وفيه دسيسة الاعتزال لقوله: القادر، لأنهم يثبتون القادرية وينفون القدرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the verse exposes their extreme misguidance and grave disbelief despite clear signs of God's power and wisdom, showing that God alone merits worship, fear of punishment, and hope for reward.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية بيان لإبعادهم في الضلال، وعظيم خطبهم في الكفر بالله، لوضوح آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barazū means they emerged from their graves to face God's judgment and reckoning.
rows.anchor: وبرزوا: أي ظهروا من قبورهم إلى جزاء الله وحسابه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Their appearing before God means they once hid shameful acts from people, thinking God did not see; on Judgment Day they recognize that nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: يستترون من العيون عند ارتكاب الفواحش، ويظنون أن ذلك خاف على الله، فإذا كان يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He explains barazū as entering the open plain, figuratively describing the whole Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وبرزوا معناه صاروا بالبراز وهي الأرض المتسعة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: He transmits philosophers' interpretation that when the soul leaves the body its covering is removed and it stands bare in its essence before God.
rows.anchor: تأويل الحكماء أن النفس إذا فارقت الجسد فكأنه زال الغطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the philosophers' reading as alien to revealed Arabic, unintelligible to Arabs, and like riddles; he calls those philosophers ignorant of God and His prophets.
rows.anchor: والعرب لا تفهم شيئا من مفاهيم أهل الفلسفة، فتفسيرهم كاللغز والأحاجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in barazū returns to all creatures being judged, and the past tense conveys certainty as if the event had already occurred.
rows.anchor: والضمير في وبرزوا عائد على الخلق المحاسبين، وعبر بلفظ الماضي لصدق المخبر به

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: He reads barazū in the passive voice with a doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: وبرزوا مبنيا للمفعول، وبتشديد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are followers and ordinary people; the arrogant are their chiefs and leaders, who led them astray and made them followers.
rows.anchor: والضعفاء: الأتباع، والعوام. وكتب بواو في المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakbarū may mean that leaders exalted themselves or that they refused to follow messengers and worship God.
rows.anchor: استكبروا تكبروا، وأظهروا تعظيم أنفسهم. أو استكبروا عن اتباع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabʿan can be a collective noun for a follower or a verbal noun like ʿadl and riḍā.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون اسم جمع لتابع، كخادم وخدم، وغائب وغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Can you relieve us?’ is a rebuke, since they know the leaders cannot help; they followed their leaders' error as directed but received no aid.
rows.anchor: وهل أنتم مغنون؟ استفهام معناه توبيخهم إياهم وتقريعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders' reply that they would have guided their followers if God had guided them is an apologetic, shamefaced return of guidance to God, and is true in itself.
rows.anchor: أجابوا بذلك على سبيل الاعتذار والخجل ورد الهداية لله تعالى، وهو كلام حق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He parses the first min as explanatory and the second as partitive, or takes both as partitive, yielding ‘some portion of some part of God's punishment.’
rows.anchor: من الأولى للتبيين، والثانية للتبعيض، كأنه قيل: هل أنتم مغنون عنا بعض الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that Zamakhsharī's explanatory min would require ‘of something’ to precede its explanation, while his two-partitive reading yields the awkward ‘part of a part’ of punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذان التوجيهان اللذان وجههما الزمخشري في من في المكانين يقتضي أولهما التقديم

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: He treats min in ‘of anything’ as extra for comprehensiveness and emphasis, while ‘of God's punishment’ depends on ‘relieve.’
rows.anchor: قال الحوفي: من عذاب الله متعلق بمغنون، ومن في من شيء لاستغراق الجنس، زائدة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He likewise calls min extra and paraphrases the question as whether they can prevent anything from them; alternatively shayʾ means relief, with ‘from God's punishment’ attached to the verb.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: ومن زائدة أي: شيئا كائنا من عذاب الله، ويكون محمولا على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative environment licenses the extra min, as though the question directly asked ‘do you relieve us?’
rows.anchor: ومسوغ الزيادة كون الخبر في سياق الاستفهام، فكأن الاستفهام دخل عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the leaders excuse themselves by claiming that had God guided them to faith they would have guided their followers, shifting responsibility for their misguidance to God as they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أجابوهم معتذرين عما كان منهم إليهم بأن الله لو هداهم إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says al-Zamakhsharī calls their excuse a lie, citing the hypocrites' false oath on resurrection; he objects that Muʿtazilites do not allow inhabitants of the Hereafter to lie.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المعتزلة لا يجوزون صدور الكذب على أهل القيامة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He offers another reading: had God placed them among those receiving divine لطف, they would have been guided and then guided their followers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: لو كنا من أهل اللطف فلطف بنا ربنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī cites al-Qāḍī's objection that this cannot mean لطف, since God has already granted it.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز حمل هذا على اللطف، لأن ذلك قد فعله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view means that, if God had rescued them from punishment and guided them to the road to Paradise, they would have guided their followers.
rows.anchor: لو خلصنا الله من العذاب وهدانا إلى طريق الجنة لهديناكم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He expands that last reading: had God shown them the way out of punishment they would have taken their followers along the path on which they had led them to ruin.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في بسط هذا القول: لو هدانا الله طريق النجاة من العذاب لهديناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested guidance is plausibly guidance to Paradise, since that is what the followers ask to receive.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ويدل على أن المراد بالهدى الهدى إلى طريق الجنة، أنه هو الذي التمسوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses the reply as ‘if God had guided us, we would have guided you.’
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لو أرشدنا الله لأرشدناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether they despair or endure says that both alternatives are equally useless to them.
rows.anchor: سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا إلى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Satan will preach to all creatures from a pulpit of fire: God truthfully promised resurrection, Paradise, Hell, and recompense, while Satan falsely denied them and broke his promise.
rows.anchor: يقف إبليس خطيبا في جهنم على منبر من نار يسمعه الخلائق جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The matter was settled’ can mean that the people of Paradise and Hell were assigned their destinations during the gathering; the intercession report supports this timing.
rows.anchor: قضي الأمر تعين قوم للجنة وقوم للنار، وذلك كله في الموقف

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the settling of the matter to be after the people of Paradise and Hell have entered their homes, an interpretation also supported here by al-Ḥasan's report.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه ما ذكرناه عن الحسن، وهو تأويل الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says the matter was finished: judgment ended and each group departed to its destination.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قضي الأمر قطع وفرغ منه، وهو الحساب، وتصادر الفريقين إلى مقربهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿd al-ḥaqq may mean a true promise, God's promise as the source of truth, or the established reality of resurrection and requital.
rows.anchor: ووعد الحق يحتمل أن يكون من إضافة الموصوف إلى صفته أي: الوعد الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading of ‘except that I called you’ is a disconnected exception, since an invitation and whispering are not clear proof or authority.
rows.anchor: وإلا أن دعوتكم الظاهر أنه استثناء منقطع، لأن دعاءه إياهم إلى الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different meaning of sulṭān is coercive power: Satan did not compel or frighten them but merely presented an option they chose.
rows.anchor: قيل: ويحتمل أن يريد بالسلطان الغلبة والتسليط والقدرة أي: ما اضطررتكم ولا خوفتكم بقوة مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes the exception connected: influence may be coercion or strengthening a desire by whispering, a type of Satanic control.
rows.anchor: القدرة على حمل الإنسان على الشيء تارة يكون بالقهر من الحامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is also taken to show that Satan cannot physically seize people, deform their bodies, or remove their reason.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن الشيطان لا قدرة له على صرع الإنسان وتعويج أعضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the verb ‘they blame me’ in the third person, a rhetorical shift referring to their conduct; they should blame themselves for poor judgment and accepting the call without evidence.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: فلا يلوموني بالياء على الغيبة، وهو التفات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says they should blame themselves for being deceived and obeying Satan instead of God; this supports human choice of salvation or damnation, with God only enabling and Satan only embellishing—a Muʿtazilite position.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن الإنسان هو الذي يختار الشقاوة والسعادة ويحصلها لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputed final yāʾ reading is attested with sukūn after a long vowel, as readers also do in maḥyāy; grammarians should not condemn it as erroneous or ugly, since linguists record it as a rarely used dialect.
rows.anchor: قد روى سكون الياء بعد الألف. وقرأ بذلك القراء نحو: محياي

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: He identifies the pronunciation as a dialect of Banū Yarbuʿ.
rows.anchor: ونص قطرب على أنها لغة في بني يربوع

rows.speaker: القاسم بن معن
rows.claim: The leading Kufan grammarian says the reading is correct.
rows.anchor: وقال القاسم بن معن وهو من رؤساء النحويين الكوفيين: هي صواب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: In response to grammarians who called it faulty, he says it is allowed; its vowel may be high or low, and he specifically calls the kasra good.
rows.anchor: فقال: هي جائزة. وقال أيضا: لا تبالي إلى أسفل حركتها، أو إلى فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān dismisses Abū Ḥātim's objection to Abū ʿAmr's approval, emphasizing that Abū ʿAmr was a master of language, grammar, and recitation and an authentic Arab.
rows.anchor: فأبو عمرو إمام لغة، وإمام نحو، وإمام قراءة، وعربي صريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by al-Nābigha demonstrates the kasra on the yāʾ in ʿalayya.
rows.anchor: وقد رووا بيت النابغة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘I disavow your associating me before,’ mā is infinitival and min qabl attaches to ‘you associated me’: Satan repudiates their making him a partner in worldly life, paralleling other verses.
rows.anchor: وما في بما أشركتموني مصدرية، ومن قبل متعلق بأشركتموني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes mā relative, meaning the idol they associated with Satan, with the relative pronoun's object omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: موصولة بمعنى الذي، والتقدير: كفرت بالصنم الذي أشركتمونيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse attaches min qabl to ‘I disavow’ and takes mā as relative: Satan had disavowed the one they made his partner when he refused to bow to Adam; Abū Ḥayyān objects that mā is not normally used for a particular rational being.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من قبل متعلق بكفرت، وما بمعنى الذي أي: كفرت من قبل حين أبيت السجود لآدم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He compares the use of mā for God to the phrase ‘Glory be to what subjected these for us’; Abū Ḥayyān says those who reject it treat subḥān as a proper name for glorification.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ونحو ما هذه يعني في إطلاقها على الله ما في قولهم: سبحان ما سخركن لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is a temporal infinitive, Satan admits that his own first sin preceded theirs.
rows.anchor: وما مصدرية ظرفية، ويكون ذلك من إبليس إقرارا على نفسه بكفره الأقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that wrongdoers face painful punishment apparently completes Satan's speech and is a warning to hearers to imagine that scene and prepare; it may instead be the keepers' or God's speech.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه من تمام كلام إبليس، حكى الله عنه ما سيقوله في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He reports the unusual nominative reading kalimatun ṭayyibatun as a subject, with ka-shajarah as its predicate; it may instead be a predicate whose subject is elided (‘the parable is a good word’).
rows.anchor: وقرىء شاذا كلمة طيبة بالرفع. قال أبو البقاء: على الابتداء، وكشجرة خبره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the good word as ‘there is no god but God.’
rows.anchor: والكلمة الطيبة هي: لا له إلا الله قاله ان عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: They identify the good word as faith.
rows.anchor: أو الإيمان قاله مجاهد وابن جريج

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي والربيع
rows.claim: They identify the good word as the believer himself.
rows.anchor: أو المؤمن نفسه قال عطية العوفي والربيع

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: He takes the good word to mean all acts of obedience or the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أو جميع طاعاته أو القرآن قاله الأصم

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: He interprets it as the call of Islam; other reported explanations are praising God and declaring His transcendence.
rows.anchor: أو دعوة الإسلام قاله ابن بحر، أو الثناء على الله أو التسبيح والتنزيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the good tree as the believer, the coconut palm, or a tree in Paradise.
rows.anchor: والشجرة الطيبة المؤمن قاله ابن عباس، أو جوزة الهند قاله علي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأنس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Most interpreters identify the good tree as a date palm.
rows.anchor: أو النخلة وعليه أكثر المتأولين وهو قول: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وأنس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: A report he relates from the Prophet, collected by al-Dāraquṭnī, says that after the Prophet recited the verse, Ibn ʿUmar felt its tree was a date palm; the excerpt gives no grading.
rows.anchor: من حديث ابن عمر مما خرجه الدارقطني عنه قال: قرأ رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو العالية وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says Anas served dates and called the palm the good tree; he also recounts the Prophet reciting the verse over a ṣāʿ of unripe dates, with a similar report in al-Tirmidhī.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: أتيت أنس بن مالك فجيء بطبق عليه رطب فقال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He generalizes the simile to any fruit-bearing tree with good produce, such as a date palm, fig, grape, or pomegranate.
rows.anchor: كل شجرة مثمرة طيبة الثمار كالنخلة، وشجرة التين، والعنب، والرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet compared a believer who recites Qurʾān to a citron, there is no objection to comparing the believer to its tree as well.
rows.anchor: وقد شبه الرسول المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن بالأترجة، فلا يبعد أن يشبه أيضا بشجرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Its root is fixed’ means that it is firmly anchored in the earth.
rows.anchor: أصلها ثابت أي: في الأرض ضارب بعروقه فيها

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: He reads ‘like a good tree, its root fixed’ with the adjective placed on the tree in wording, although the root is its real bearer; the common reading assigns rootedness to the cause lexically and semantically and balances fixed roots with a high top.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نس بن مالك: كشجرة طيبة ثابت أصلها، أجريت الصفة على الشجرة لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘branch’ means its top and crown; although a real tree has branches, the singular uses the generic category, and ‘in heaven’ means upward, not under a roof.
rows.anchor: يريد بالفرع أعلاها ورأسها، وإن كان المشبه به ذا فروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says God created Adam with a height of sixty cubits extending into the sky.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «خلق الله آدم طوله في السماء ستون ذراعا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good word is rooted in believers' hearts; good deeds grow from it and ascend to God (35:10), and the resulting reward is its fruit.
rows.anchor: كانت الكلمة أصلها ثابت في قلوب أهل الإيمان، وما يصدر عنها من الأفعال الزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree's four qualities are goodness, rootedness, height, and continuous fruit: good means noble origin and pleasant taste.
rows.anchor: ووصف هذه الشجرة بأربعة أوصاف: الأول قوله: طيبة، أي كريمة المنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line of poetry uses ṭayyib for an easy, wholesome dwelling or place.
rows.anchor: طيب الباءة سهل ولهم ... سبل إن شئت في وحش وعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firm roots signify stability, resistance to wind, longevity, and the joy of finding what endures.
rows.anchor: الثاني: رسوخ أصلها، وذلك يدل على تمكنها، وأن الرياح لا تقصفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its high top signals the tree's strength, deep roots, distance from earth's impurities, and freedom from contamination.
rows.anchor: الثالث: علو فرعها، وذلك يدل على تمكن الشجرة ورسوخ عروقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its fourth quality is that fruit is continually present; ḥīn means a portion of time, and the poem illustrates its use.
rows.anchor: الرابع: ديمومة وجود ثمرتها وحضورها في كل الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree yields its fruit at every time God appoints.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: تعطي جناها كل وقت وقته الله له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: They take ‘every ḥīn’ as every year; on this basis Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād, and jurists say an oath not to do something for a ḥīn lasts one year.
rows.anchor: أي كل سنة، ولذلك قال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والحكم، وحماد

rows.speaker: علي ومجاهد
rows.claim: They are cited for an interpretation of eight months; six months is also proposed as the period fruit remains on the palm.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ثمانية أشهر قاله علي ومجاهد، ستة أشهر وهي مدة بقاء الثمر عليها

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: He says ḥīn means two months, because the date palm bears fruit for two months.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: الحين شهران، لأن النخلة تدوم مثمرة شهرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says a coconut tree bears fruit every month, so it never lacks fruit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تتعطل من ثمر تحمل في كل شهر، وهي شجرة جوز الهند

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والربيع
rows.claim: They gloss ‘every ḥīn’ as each morning and evening and whenever fruit is wanted, fitting a tree in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والضحاك، والربيع: كل حين أي كل غدوة وعشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sensory parables make intelligible meanings graspable to reason by engaging perception, imagination, and estimation, helping people reach the point being taught.
rows.anchor: التذكر المرجو بضرب المثل هو التفهم والتصور للمعاني المدركة بالعقل، فمتى أبرزت بالمحسوسات

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the evil word as unbelief.
rows.anchor: والكلمة الخبيثة هي كلمة الكفر على قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: He identifies the evil word as lying, and also describes it as promoting the call of unbelief and what is attributed to it.
rows.anchor: وقال مسروق: الكذب، وقال: أن تجر دعوة الكفر وما يعزى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition of the evil word is any speech God does not approve.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كل كلام لا يرضاه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: He reads ‘God struck a parable: an evil word’ with the word kalima in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وضرب الله مثلا كلمة خبيثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading puts mathala in the accusative, coordinated with kalimatan ṭayyibatan.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: ومثل كلمة بنصب مثل عطفا على كلمة طيبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Most identify the evil tree as colocynth; the view is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: شجرة الحنظل قاله الأكثرون: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأنس بن مالك، ورواه عن النبي

rows.speaker: الزجاج وفرقة
rows.claim: They identify it as a garlic plant.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج وفرقة: شجرة الثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications are the kashūt parasitic plant, algae, truffles, or any tree whose fruit is not good.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شجرة الكشوت، وهي شجرة لا ورق لها ولا أصل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He objects that colocynth, garlic, and the other named plants are herbs, not trees, unless the word tree is used figuratively; he notes the Prophet did call garlic and onion ‘this tree.’
rows.anchor: ويرد على هذه الأقوال أن هذه كلها من النجم وليست من الشجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He also identifies the evil tree as the disbeliever or as a tree never created on earth.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: هي الكافر، وعنه أيضا: شجرة لم تخلق على الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He prefers an unspecified tree with these traits, such as an acacia or poisonous tree: uprooted, weak, and toppled by a slight wind, seeming useful to an ignorant distant observer while its fruit is vile and useless.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والظاهر عندي أن التشبيه وقع بشجرة غير معينة، إذا وجدت منها هذه الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being uprooted above the earth contrasts with the good tree's fixed root: the evil plant has no firmly settled root and stands on the surface.
rows.anchor: واجتثت من فوق الأرض مقابل لقوله: أصلها ثابت أي: لم يتمكن لها أصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unstable tree pictures unbelief unsupported by proof and soon vanishing; truth is established by proof in the believer's heart.
rows.anchor: شبه بهذه الشجرة القول الذي لم يعضد بحجة، فهو لا يثبت بل يضمحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's confirming believers in worldly life means steadfastness through persecution; he recalls the People of the Ditch, those sawn or scraped with iron combs, and the perseverance of George, Simon, and Bilāl.
rows.anchor: لو فتنوا عن دينهم في الدنيا لثبتوا عليه وما زلوا، كما جرى لأصحاب الأخدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Hereafter believers remain composed when asked about their belief before witnesses, without hesitation, bewilderment, or being overwhelmed by the terrors of gathering.
rows.anchor: إذا سئلوا عند توافق الإشهاد عن معتقدهم ولم يتلعثموا، ولم يبهتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers meant are all believers from Adam until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: والذين آمنوا عام من لدن آدم إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: طاووس وقتادة وجمهور العلماء
rows.claim: They say God's confirming believers in worldly life lasts through a person's life, while confirmation in the Hereafter occurs at questioning in the grave; al-Ṭabarī prefers this view.
rows.anchor: وقال طاووس وقتادة وجمهور من العلماء: أن تثبيتهم في الدنيا هو مدة حياة الإنسان

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب وجماعة
rows.claim: They say worldly life here is the questioning in the grave and the Hereafter is the Day of Judgment at presentation; al-Barāʾ transmits this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب وجماعة: في الحياة الدنيا هي وقت سؤاله في قبره، ورواه البراء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take confirmation to mean remaining faithful in life and being gathered in faith, or worldly victory and Hereafter reward and Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى تثبيته في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة هو حياته على الإيمان، وحشره عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's recitation of this verse when a believer is questioned in the grave does not settle which time ‘worldly life’ or ‘Hereafter’ denotes, since the wording allows the alternatives.
rows.anchor: لا يظهر منه يعني: أن الحياة الدنيا هي حياة الإنسان، وأن الآخرة في القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuthabbit means that God keeps believers firm in faith and prevents them from slipping.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يثبت: يديمهم عليه، ويمنعهم من الزلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-qawl al-thābit apparently modifies yuthabbit; another parse connects it to āmanū.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن بالقول الثابت متعلق بقوله: يثبت. وقيل: يتعلق بآمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioning in the grave is part of Sunni belief.
rows.anchor: وسؤال العبد في قبره معتقد أهل السنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
rows.claim: His verse asks God to confirm the good bestowed on the Prophet, like confirming Moses, and to grant victory like theirs.
rows.anchor: فثبت الله ما آتاك من حسن ... تثبيت موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ẓālimūn means disbelievers, contrasted with believers; they waver in worldly trials for lack of proof and become confused in their answers in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ويضل الله الظالمين أي: الكافرين لمقابلتهم بالمؤمنين، وإضلالهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the good word and its people were described before the evil word and its people, the description of divine treatment follows the same order.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم تشبيه الكلمة الطيبة على تشبيه الكلمة الخبيثة، تقدم في هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's assignment of each group is His will and cannot be challenged; He is not questioned about what He does.
rows.anchor: ذكر أنه لا يمكن اعتراض فيما خص به كل واحد منهما، إذ ذاك راجع إلى مشيئته تعالى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says God's will follows wisdom: He supports and protects believers as they stand firm, while leaving wrongdoers to themselves when they stumble.
rows.anchor: مشيئة الله تابعة للحكمة من تثبيت المؤمنين وتأييدهم وعصمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one syntactic analysis, an omitted ‘gratitude’ is the object replaced by unbelief and takes the deleted preposition bi; without the omitted noun, the preposition is understood to have entered niʿmat before deletion.
rows.anchor: شكر نعمة الله، فهو الذي دخلت عليه الباء ثم حذفت، وإذا لم يقدر مضاف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They made their people settle’ means the people who followed them in disbelief.
rows.anchor: وأحلوا قومهم أي: من تابعهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: They incorrectly make kufran the second object of baddalū; with this verb, the object governed by a preposition is second and the direct object is first.
rows.anchor: وزعم الحوفي وأبو البقاء أن كفرا هو مفعول ثان لبدلوا، وليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: They parse Hell as an appositive to the Abode of Ruin; al-Zamakhsharī calls it an explanatory apposition, making the settlement in the Hereafter. Ibn Zayd identifies the Abode of Ruin as Hell.
rows.anchor: وأعرب الحوفي وأبو البقاء: جهنم بدلا من دار البوار، والزمخشري عطف بيان

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: One report from ʿAlī identifies the Abode of Ruin as the Battle of Badr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عن علي يوم بدر

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: He says the verse was revealed about those killed at Badr, with the Abode of Ruin being earthly destruction such as Badr's well and other killing sites.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء بن يسار: نزلت في قتلى بدر، فيكون دار البوار أي: الهلاك في الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: For the earthly-destruction reading, they parse Jahannam as an accusative on the construction ‘as for Hell, they enter it’; Ibn Abī ʿAbla's nominative reading can instead be a predicate of an omitted subject, which Abū Ḥayyān prefers over the less-supported accusative.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا أعرب ابن عطية وأبو البقاء: جهنم منصوب على الاشتغال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the accusative analysis, yuṣallūnahā has no syntactic position; with the other analysis it may be circumstantial of Hell, the Abode of Ruin, or the people. The subject of ‘evil is the abode’ is omitted and means Hell.
rows.anchor: وعلى تأويل الاشتغال يكون يصلونها لا موضع له من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivals are idols whom the disbelievers added as gods besides God, compounding their ingratitude for His favor.
rows.anchor: جعلوا لله أندادا أي زادوا إلى كفرهم نعمته أن صيروا له أندادا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the lām in liyuḍillū with fatḥa, while the other seven readers use ḍamma; the same difference occurs in 22:9, 31:6, and 30:29.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمر: وليضلوا هنا، وليضل في الحج ولقمان والروم بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām apparently marks outcome: making rivals results in misguidance or leading others astray, resembling a purpose clause; one view says fatḥa excludes the outcome meaning, while ḍamma allows either outcome or purpose.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن اللام لام الصيرورة والمآل. لما كانت نتيجة جعل الأنداد آلهة الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to enjoy life is a threat and warning, like ‘do whatever you will.’
rows.anchor: والأمر بالتمتع أمر تهديد ووعيد على حد قوله: اعملوا ما شئتم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the threat ironically depicts them as so immersed in present enjoyment that they seem commanded by an irresistible master, with no interest in what follows.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: تمتعوا إيذان بأنهم لانغماسهم في التمتع بالحاضر، وأنهم لا يعرفون غيره

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He cites the poetic phrase ‘Muḥammad, every soul would ransom you’ as evidence for the construction, while noting that it is permitted only in poetry.
rows.anchor: محمد تفد نفسك كل نفس أنشده سيبويه إلا أنه قال: إن هذا لا يجوز إلا في الشعر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says deletion of the lām is allowed because the command ‘say’ compensates for it; deleting it with no preceding command would be impermissible.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في هذا القول: وإنما جاز حذف اللام لأن الأمر الذي هو قل، عوض منه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: He estimates ‘tell them: perform prayer’ followed by ‘they will perform it’ as the answer; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because conditional response should differ in verb or subject and the estimate repeats the same third-person verb after an addressee command.
rows.anchor: وذهب المبرد إلى أن التقدير: قل لهم أقيموا يقيموا، فيقيموا المصرح به جواب أقيموا المحذوف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية عن سيبويه
rows.claim: He transmits Sibawayh's alternative estimate: ‘if you tell them, perform prayer, they will perform it.’
rows.anchor: التقدير أن تقل لهم أقيموا يقيموا قاله سيبويه فيما حكاه ابن عطية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He treats the command as carrying an implied condition, as in ‘obey God and He will admit you to Paradise’; unlike the previous analysis, the condition follows the command.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: جواب الأمر معه شرط مقدر تقول: أطع الله يدخلك الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو علي وفرقة
rows.claim: They take yuqīmū as a present-tense indicative form used with command meaning; Abū Ḥayyān objects that command meaning normally keeps the nūn, while Abū ʿAlī compares its deletion to a noun built in address.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مضارع بلفظ الخبر صرف عن لفظ الأمر، والمعنى: أقيموا، قاله أبو علي وفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In these syntactic analyses, the quoted or estimated command concerns establishing prayer and giving; Ibn ʿAṭiyya instead makes it convey the whole sacred law, which is broader.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق القول الملفوظ به أو المقدر في هذه التخاريج هو الأمر بالإقامة والإنفاق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He suggests that the words spoken are the following verse, ‘God, who created the heavens and the earth’; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as disrupting the syntax and leaving the prayer clause detached or awkwardly inserted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويظهر أن المقول هو الآية التي بعد أعني قوله: الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Prayer can mean every obligatory and voluntary prayer or specifically the five obligatory prayers; Ibn ʿAbbās gives the latter interpretation and glosses spending as obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: وأن يراد بها الخمس، وبذلك فسرها ابن عباس: وفسر الإنفاق بزكاة الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar and meaning of secret and open spending were discussed at the end of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وتقدم إعراب سرا وعلانية وشرحها في أواخر البقرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He glosses bayʿ as giving in exchange and khilāl as friendship or mutual affection, the verbal noun of khālaltu; a line by Imruʾ al-Qays illustrates khilāl.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: البيع هنا البذل، والخلال المخالة، وهو مصدر من خاللت خلالا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He says khilāl is the plural of khulla.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الخلال جمع خلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qirāʾa dispute over lā bayʿun fīhi wa-lā khilāl, with nominative or accusative, was already treated at 2:254; the day is Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الخلاف في قراءة لا بيع فيه ولا خلال بالفتح أو بالرفع في البقرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: People exchange money and give gifts expecting equivalents or something better, but only sincere believers spend purely for God's sake; they are urged to do so because no sale or friendship will benefit them on that day.
rows.anchor: وأما الإنفاق لوجه الله خالصا كقوله: وما لا حد عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing the blessed and the wretched, Abū Ḥayyān says happiness comes through knowing God and His attributes while misery comes through ignorance, so the passage closes with proofs of the Creator's existence, knowledge, and power.
rows.anchor: ولما أطال تعالى الكلام في وصف أحوال السعداء والأشقياء، وكان حصول السعادة بمعرفة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gives ten kinds of evidence: it begins with the originating creation of the heavens and earth and states the remaining proofs in separate clauses to show each is independently probative.
rows.anchor: وذكر عشرة أنواع من الدلائل فذكر أولا إبداعه وإنشاء السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allāh is the subject and alladhī is its predicate.
rows.anchor: والله مرفوع على الابتداء، والذي خبره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says whoever believes and inwardly accepts this statement will believe, pray, and spend, linking the command to the next description of God as Creator.
rows.anchor: ومن أخبر بهذه الجملة وتقررت في نفسه آمن وصلى وأنفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn ʿAṭiyya's parse, the prayer command becomes an answer to ‘Tell My servants: God who created the heavens and earth’; Abū Ḥayyān objects that this fragments the syntax.
rows.anchor: فكأنه يقول: يقيموا الصلاة، جواب لقوله: قل لعبادي الله الذي خلق السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘He brought forth for you provision,’ the apparent object is rizqan and min is partitive, making the phrase circumstantial: some fruit is provision while some is harmful.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن مفعول أخرج هو رزقا لكم، ومن للتبعيض

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
rows.claim: They allow min to explain the kind, making the fruit itself the provision; Abū Ḥayyān objects that explanatory min follows an ambiguous expression that it explains.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون من لبيان الجنس قاله ابن عطية والزمخشري

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He alternatively parses ‘from the fruits’ as the direct object and rizqan as a circumstantial accusative or cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون من الثمرات مفعول أخرج، ورزقا حالا من المفعول

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Some call min extra; most Basrans reject that because what precedes it is affirmative and what follows is definite, though al-Akhfash permits it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من زائدة، وهذا لا يجوز عند جمهور البصريين، لأن ما قبلها واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-fulk is a plural, which accounts for the feminine plural verb tajrī.
rows.anchor: والفلك هنا جمع فلك، ولذلك قال: لتجري

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He takes ‘by His command’ to mean by God's utterance ‘Be.’
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لقوله، كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subjugating ships entails subjugating seas and winds; rivers are made useful by their flow and by opening channels through them.
rows.anchor: وانطوى في تسخير الفلك تسخير البحار، وتسخير الرياح. وأما تسخير الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾibayn is circumstantial: the sun and moon continuously travel and shine, helping the earth, bodies, and plants.
rows.anchor: وانتصب دائبين على الحال والمعنى: يدأبان في سيرهما وإنارتهما

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss that the sun and moon persist in obedience to God; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is sound if obedience means their submission through being subjugated, since that is already stated, or if it means deliberate worship like human worship.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حبان يرفعه إلى ابن عباس أنه قال: معناه دائبين في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are subjugated by alternating in succession to serve sleep and livelihood.
rows.anchor: وتسخير الليل والنهار كونهما يتعاقبان خلفه للمنام والمعاش

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians call the subjection of night and day metaphorical because accidents cannot literally be subjugated.
rows.anchor: وقال المتكلمون: تسخير الليل والنهار مجاز، لأنهما عرضان، والأعراض لا تسخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to humankind means the species collectively received every sort of thing people might request and benefit from, though no individual has all blessings; they are distributed among people.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للجنس من البشر أي: أن الإنسان قد أوتي من كل ما شأن أن يسأل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والحسن ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد وعمرو بن قائد وقتادة وسلام ويعقوب ونافع
rows.claim: They read min kull with nunation, meaning from every one of the created things just mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، والضحاك، والحسن، ومحمد بن علي، وجعفر بن محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading mā is relative and a second object: everything that can be requested for benefit; another takes mā as negative and min kull as the second object, meaning blessings people never requested.
rows.anchor: وما موصولة مفعول ثان أي: ما شأنه أن يسأل بمعنى يطلب الانتفاع به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
rows.claim: They give the negative mā interpretation, which reports God's abundant gifts that people did not ask for; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it al-Ḍaḥḥāk's explanation.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول بدأ به الزمخشري، وثنى به ابن عطية وقال: إنه تفسير الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That negative reading conflicts with the common genitive reading min kulli mā saʾaltumūhu, which instead says people asked; al-Zamakhsharī resolves this by taking the request as need expressed by the state of things.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفسير يظهر أنه مناف لقراءة الجمهور من كل ما سألتموه بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may also be infinitival; the pronoun in saʾaltumūhu then refers to God, while on a relative reading it refers to the requested thing and its omitted relative link cannot be restored in either proposed form.
rows.anchor: والضمير في سألتموه إن كانت ما مصدرية عائد على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: He explains niʿma as a noun used in place of the verbal noun inʿām, so it is not pluralized because it functions as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي: اسم أقيم مقام المصدر، يقال: أنعم إنعاما ونعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿma apparently means the bestowed blessing, a collective generic noun rather than one blessing; iḥṣāʾ means to enumerate or encompass, and detailed counting is beyond people and known only to God.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن النعمة هو المنعم به، وأنه هو اسم جنس لا يراد به الواحد

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: He says a person who sees God's blessing only in food and drink has little knowledge and faces punishment.
rows.anchor: من لم ير نعمة الله عليه إلا في مطعمه ومشربه فقد قل علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm ends by calling the human unjust and ungrateful because the preceding verses condemn exchanging God's blessing for disbelief and setting up rivals.
rows.anchor: تقدم قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وبعده، وجعلوا لله أندادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naḥl instead ends the reminder of many favors by contrasting the Creator with what cannot create and pointing to forgiveness and mercy, encouraging people to return to God.
rows.anchor: وأما في النحل فلما ذكر عدة تفضلات، وأطنب فيها، وقال: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different endings suit giver and recipient: God gives and forgives or shows mercy, while humans respond with injustice and ingratitude; God may forgive their wrong and show mercy for their failures.
rows.anchor: فحصل من المنعم ما يناسبه حالة عطائه وهو الغفران والرحمة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: He is cited by al-Sakhāwī for saying Ibrāhīm's ending was abrogated by the ending in al-Naḥl; Abū Ḥayyān dismisses the abrogation claim.
rows.anchor: ودعوى إن هذه الآية منسوخة بآية النحل لا يلتفت إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humankind generically shows injustice by neglecting gratitude and disbelief by denying blessings.
rows.anchor: يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها، ويكفرها بجحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls people unjust in hardship because they complain and despair, and ungrateful in prosperity because they hoard and withhold.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ظلوم في الشدة فيشكو ويجزع، كفار في النعمة يجمع ويمنع

none: Qurʾānic verse text only; no commentary point is stated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding account of the earth's submission to God's will underscores that God alone controls it; the prohibition on taking two gods necessarily prohibits taking multiple gods.
rows.anchor: الأرض لما يريده تعالى منها، فكان هو المتفرد بذلك. نهى أن يشرك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular or dual noun can be used generically, as in praise of ‘the man’ or ‘the two men’; the poem about kindling fire with two sticks illustrates this usage, after which ‘two’ and ‘one’ emphasize the exact numbers.
rows.anchor: أكد الموضوع لهما بالوصف، فقيل: إلهين اثنين، وقيل: إله واحد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says nouns for singular and dual express both kind and a specific number, so adding ‘two’ or ‘one’ stresses the intended number; without ‘one,’ ‘He is a god’ might establish divinity without affirming uniqueness.
rows.anchor: الاسم الحامل لمعنى الإفراد أو التثنية دال على شيئين: على الجنسية، والعدد المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tattakhidhū apparently governs one object, with ithnayn as its emphasized apposition; alternatives make the verb govern two objects with the second preceding, or omit a second object meaning ‘as deity.’
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن لا تتخذوا، تعدى إلى واحد واثنين كما تقدم تأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impossibility of two gods is established through several arguments in works of theology.
rows.anchor: وتقرير منافاة الاثنينية للإلهية من وجوه ذكرت في علم أصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God affirms that He alone is God using restriction and explicit emphasis on oneness; shifting from third person to direct address intensifies the command to fear Him.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى أنه إله واحد كما قال: وإلهكم إله واحد بأداة الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyyāya is the object of an omitted verb placed after it and indicated by farhabūn; Ibn ʿAṭiyya's proposed preposing of the verb is grammatically mistaken, since a detached pronoun object must follow its verb except in poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وانتصب إياي بفعل محذوف مقدر التأخير عنه يدل عليه فارهبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns all that is in the heavens and earth because He is the one necessary God, and everything else exists through His creation.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما كان هو الإله الواحد الواجب لذاته كان ما سواه موجودا بإيجاده وخلقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses dīn as sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: الدين الإخلاص

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: He glosses dīn as worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: العبادة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He glosses dīn as the testimony that none is god but God, observance of the prescribed limits, and religious duties.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وإقامة الحدود والفرائض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
rows.claim: They gloss dīn as obedience; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds sovereignty or dominion, supported by a poem using the word for obedience and rule.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري وابن عطية: الطاعة، زاد ابن عطية: والملك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says wāṣib means perpetual and enduring, without cessation, referring to reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: والواصب الواجب الثابت لأن كل نعمة منه بالطاعة واجبة له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والحسن ومجاهد والضحاك وقتادة وابن زيد والثوري
rows.claim: They gloss wāṣib as lasting forever.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، والحسن، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وقتادة، وابن زيد، والثوري: واصبا دائما

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He derives wāṣib from the root for exertion or fatigue, as a relational adjective meaning ‘possessing exertion.’
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن الأنباري أنه من الوصب وهو التعب، وهو على معنى النسب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He also says dīn is a burdensome duty, explaining why religious obligation is called taklīf.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو وله الدين ذا كلفة ومشقة، ولذلك سمي تكليفا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says obedience belongs to God whether the servant finds what is commanded easy or difficult; waṣb is severe fatigue.
rows.anchor: وله الدين والطاعة رضي العبد بما يؤمر به وسهل عليه أم لا يسهل

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: He glosses wāṣib as pure or sincere.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: واصبا خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the wāw in ‘and His is the religion’ a new beginning, but Abū Ḥayyān says grammarians use that label only for circumstantial wāw, which does not fit here; the wāw is conjunctive, either to the predicate or the whole sentence.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال واو ابتداء إلا لواو الحال، ولا يظهر هنا الحال، وإنما هي عاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāṣiban is circumstantial, governed by the element on which the prepositional phrase depends.
rows.anchor: وانتصب واصبا على الحال، والعامل فيها هو ما يتعلق به المجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘Will you fear anyone other than God?’ rebukes people who know His oneness and their dependence on Him yet fear one who cannot help or harm them.
rows.anchor: أفغير الله استفهام تضمن التوبيخ والتعجب أي: بعد ما عرفتم وحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every blessing people acquire is created by God, indicating the duty to thank Him for worldly and religious blessings; compare 16:18.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى بأن جميع النعم المكتسبة منا إنما هي من إيجاده واختراعه، ففيه إشارة إلى وجوب الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is relative, connected to you by bi-kum, with min niʿmat explaining it and fa-min Allāh as its predicate; estimating a specific verb such as ‘settled’ or ‘came down’ is unsound.
rows.anchor: وما موصولة، وصلتها بكم، والعامل فعل الاستقرار أي: وما استقر بكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Ḥūfī allow mā to be conditional with an elided verb, which al-Farrāʾ estimates as ‘whatever blessing occurs to you.’ Abū Ḥayyān begins to reject this as very weak.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الفراء والحوفي: أن تكون ما شرطية، وحذف فعل الشرط. قال الفراء: التقدير
